corrected_value.title: "One of us": Outstanding willingness to help save a single identified compatriot

decisions.location: Results (line 54); see also Introduction (lines 3, 28-29), Discussion (lines 69, 83, 85), and References (line 304)
decisions.quote: In our extension, we failed to find support for the findings by Kogut and Ritov (2007) that there is a higher likelihood of helping single victims over a group if they belong to the ingroup (vs. the outgroup).
decisions.reason: The paper explicitly designs and reports a pre-registered conceptual replication of Kogut and Ritov (2007) alongside its close replication of Kogut and Ritov (2005a) Study 2 by adding identified ingroup (American) and identified outgroup (Russian) conditions crossed with victim singularity (single child vs. group of eight children) in a 2 x 4 between-subjects design (N = 1,835), and directly tests and compares its results against Kogut and Ritov's (2007) finding that singularity and group belonging interact to produce higher willingness to help a single identified ingroup victim over a group (lines 3, 28-29, 37, 54, 69, 83, 85). The reference list (line 304) and Crossref metadata verify the original identity as Kogut, T., & Ritov, I. (2007), '"One of us": Outstanding willingness to help save a single identified compatriot', Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes 104(2): 150-157, DOI 10.1016/j.obhdp.2007.04.006. The only shipped row (input_row_index 1473, DOI 10.1002/bdm.492) is Kogut and Ritov (2005a), 'The "identified victim" effect: an identified group, or just a single individual?', Journal of Behavioral Decision Making 18(3): 157-167 (target_index 0), which did not manipulate ingroup/outgroup belonging (line 31). Because the 2007 article reports distinct experiments in a different journal two years later, report equivalence does not apply and this target is genuinely absent from the shipped rows. No prior adjudication or prior state file existed for this work.
